items.note: The event-loop item is html-css-js-final-mcq-22. Its key feedback at line 180 says 'Code after an await resumes as a microtask on the single main thread', matching the event-loop page's cheat sheet. The wording 'resumes as a task' no longer appears.

The grid item is html-css-js-final-mcq-03 (lines 21-26). The untaught repeat(4, 25%) distractor is gone (no '25%' anywhere in the bank). The distractors repeat(4, 225px) (line 22), repeat(auto-fill, 225px) (line 23) and 4fr (line 25) are all settled by the same taught idea that gaps take space between columns, and Chromium confirms each feedback. repeat(4, 225px): scrollWidth 948. auto-fill: three 225px columns with the fourth image wrapped. repeat(4, 1fr): four 213px columns, no overflow. 4fr: one 900px column.

html-css-js-final-mcq-23: the dialog distractor at line 185 is rejected with the accessibility page's own trap definition (Tab, Shift+Tab or Escape cannot move focus out). It no longer appeals to an untaught 'expected dialog pattern', so only the Brightness note is defensible.
The fetch(...).json() item and its 'request is read' feedback are not in the bank: grep finds neither 'request is read' nor 'json method'.

No item claims that the Network panel shows 200 for a CORS-blocked response; grep finds no 'Network panel shows the server answered'. The CORS slot is now html-css-js-final-mcq-29 (lines 239-244): server.proxy missing in production, with a 404 from the static server. It is consistent with the CORS page.
html-css-js-final-mcq-26 (lines 211-220) ends the chain at catch (line 215), so no option depends on a then running after catch. Node 24 prints 'B too big 6', matching the key at line 216.
html-css-js-final-mcq-23, line 183: Help is 'an a element with an href, holding only an icon, with aria-label="Help"; Tab reaches it', so it is a real, focusable link and not a second barrier.
The BigInt id item is gone; no 'BigInt' appears in the bank. Position 19 (lines 148-156) is the 7 / 2 port. Node 24 prints 3.5, 1, 2, 3, matching the key at line 155.

html-css-js-final-mcq-25: line 201 sends headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" }, so the ignored result object is the only defect. Node 24 with a stubbed 400 prints 'Saved', matching the key at line 206.

html-css-js-final-mcq-12: the stem at line 94 puts the page and the API together at http://staging.example.com, so distractor B at line 96 (SameSite=Strict) is settled as same-site. The key feedback at line 98 says browsers do not keep a Secure cookie that arrives over HTTP, matching the Chromium check: the cookie jar stayed empty and later requests carried no Cookie header.

html-css-js-final-mcq-30: the stem at line 246 declares button and note ('note is a status paragraph'), and the snippet uses note.textContent (lines 247 and 249), so window.status no longer applies. Chromium rerun with an explicit note element: a requestAnimationFrame loop over a real click and a 3-second synchronous loop recorded 55 frames with only 'Idle' then 'Done', never 'Working...'; the click returned after about 3.1 s. That matches the key at line 251. The new distractor at line 253 ('Only Working...') is refuted by the same run, and its feedback is accurate. A diff against the loop-3 bytes (9c4f8913...) shows changes only on lines 246, 247, 249, 250 and 253, all inside item 30.
